iterations.note: Iteration 2's raw score was 5. Its sole finding is marked late:true by the critic itself and was overruled entirely, so the late-excluded score is 10. Both numbers are recorded rather than one replacing the other.

arbitration_of_the_late_finding: OVERRULED, and the finding is simply wrong. bible/timeline.md, Day 8-9: 'Hale leaves the theodolite set up on Sile Head overnight rather than lose the sight; at dawn it faces the church tower. At that same dawn an entry is taken at the Raven Hause station...' bible/mysteries.md is more explicit: 'Hale spent the night of Day 8 on Sile Head to keep his sight. Silas Brock came up at first light with the field book... and walked him across to the Raven Hause station.' Two places, two events, and the walk between them is the point of the scene. The draft has exactly that. It was the critic that conflated the landmarks, not the draft. The orchestrator verified the wording against both bible files by grep before overruling rather than deciding from memory. Recorded in specs/loops/LOOP-003/late_findings.jsonl.
resolution: Both iteration-1 findings addressed by literal substitution; neither skipped, neither quoted string surviving.
gap: This is the clearest instance in the run of a model critic producing a confident, high-severity, wholly false finding on a second read of text it had already passed. Acting on it would have moved a canonical event to the wrong hill and broken two earlier chapters.
